content: Certain phenomena, such as specific barriers to accessing vaccination and the treatment of particular groups by healthcare services, require detailed investigation to understand their impact on vaccine uptake. The findings of a report are more likely to influence outcomes if the research team actively involves key stakeholders in the planning of data collection, hypothesis generation, and drafting of reports. This collaborative approach not only raises the profile of the work but also highlights other relevant studies, enabling cross-comparison of findings. For more complex analyses, consulting experienced researchers is recommended. When resources for data collection are limited, sharing anonymized data between programs and researchers can maximize the utility of available resources and enhance the impact of the data. It is advisable to share plans and materials and engage in discussions with the following groups: Other stakeholders, who can provide broad expertise, contextual insights, and resource mobilization. Experienced researchers, who can offer informal peer reviews of the data, suggest connections with other datasets or established knowledge, and often lead to deeper analyses and new findings. Input from the target population, which can improve the quality of analysis and serve as a validated method for interpreting results. The WHO policy on data sharing is detailed in Annex 7 for further reference. The BeSD (Behavioral and Social Drivers) tools are designed to generate data and use findings to increase vaccine uptake. These tools can be applied at various levels of immunization programs for planning, monitoring, and guiding intervention design in specific settings. Data should also be shared with National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) to support evidence-based recommendations. The BeSD framework identifies four main domains influencing vaccine uptake: thinking and feeling, social processes, motivation, and practical issues. Priority indicators for tracking these factors over time are included in the tool annexes. Data generated from these tools can be used to: Inform the design and evaluation of interventions to increase vaccine uptake. Develop targeted interventions to address context-specific drivers and barriers, particularly for disadvantaged populations. Evaluate the effectiveness of strategies and monitor trends over time through routine BeSD assessments. Advocate for and mobilize resources. Contribute to comparative analyses with other data sources to provide a comprehensive understanding of issues and guide program planning. When planning interventions, four foundational areas are critical to any immunization program: 1. Community engagement. 2. Communication and education. 3. Provider recommendations, reminders, and inclusive services. 4. Policy requirements and incentives. BeSD assessments can help identify why interventions may not be working, particularly through qualitative interview guides. At the subnational level, these assessments can be integrated into human-centered design processes to diagnose reasons for low uptake, select tailored interventions, and evaluate their effectiveness. Monitoring and evaluation of interventions using BeSD indicators are essential to determine whether the interventions achieve their intended outcomes and to guide continuous improvement. Indicators should be selected carefully to measure desired changes and analyzed to inform decisions and actions. Triangulating BeSD data with other data sources, such as surveillance data, census data, and health system data, can provide a more complete understanding of vaccination gaps and inform tailored interventions. For example: Surveillance data can identify high-burden areas for prioritization. Census data can contextualize vaccine uptake in relation to socio-demographic characteristics. Health system data can highlight trends and patterns in the uptake of other child health services compared to immunization services. Social listening data can track public conversations and misinformation about vaccination, providing insights into effective messaging strategies. Accountability is critical throughout all assessments. Regular consultation with participating communities and stakeholders, along with sharing indicator data, ensures transparency and tracks progress over time.
